newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Rebels kill two soldiers in southern Senegal.
newsitem.headline: Rebels kill two soldiers in southern Senegal.

text.p: Separatist rebels in Senegal's troubled Casamance province have killed two soldiers in the worst ceasefire breach for many months, military sources reported on Monday.
Rebel sources told Reuters they were investigating Sunday's incident but denied they had called off a self-imposed ceasefire in the 15-year-old rebellion.
"Rebels of the MFDC (Movement of Democratic Forces of Casamance) attacked an army unit stationed at the village of Djirack and killed two soldiers," the military sources said.
An army spokesman said troops returning fire killed a number of rebels but declined to say how many.
An official source in the provincial capital, Ziguinchor, said by telephone at least 30 rebels were killed.
Hundreds of people have died in Casamance since the MFDC started fighting for independence in 1982.
In December 1995 the movement's main figurehead, Catholic churchman Diamacoune Senghor, declared a unilateral ceasefire.
The ceasefire has been broadly respected since then although two government soldiers were killed in Casamance last January when they drove over a land mine.
On March 17, clashes were reported between soldiers and rebels of the MFDC, close to the border with Guinea Bissau.
A source close to Senghor said the MFDC's civilian wing was investigating Sunday's killings.

"In any case we will not call off our unilateral ceasefire," the source said. The rebels deny they are split between a faction backing negotiations with the Dakar government and another wanting to pursue armed rebellion.
